patch.value: Research the latest official Home Assistant action APIs and the configured current server; correct transport-specific response typing; expose explicit target and response controls; preserve legacy command compatibility; validate setup, formats, schema, help, packaging, release automation, and private live execution without persisting identifiers.
Unify typed service action execution across REST and WebSocket

Provide a stable, type-safe, agent-oriented service action contract across Home Assistant REST and WebSocket transports, including response capability discovery, explicit targets, safe dry runs, strict validation, and normalized output.

call-service models current REST changed-state and service-response results plus WebSocket context/response results without any or guessed types; Agents can inspect and dry-run normalized requests, target selectors, transport choice, validation, and response capability before mutation; HASSIO_READONLY accepts explicit true and false values consistently through the complete Commander program; All source coverage and docstrings remain 100/100/100/100, every source file stays within 300 code lines, all formats and recursive help validate, and live evidence contains no private identifiers
Official REST and WebSocket docs, installed Commander/Undici types, live service schemas, prior PM lineage, and duplicate inventory reviewed
Let agents plan, validate, execute, and interpret Home Assistant actions without transport-specific ambiguity.
Eliminates incorrectly typed REST results, improves target precision, prevents unsafe environment parsing surprises, and makes response-required services reliable.
One documented call-service workflow produces a stable envelope across REST and WebSocket and supports non-executing plans.

The current 2026.7.4 server exposes many response-capable actions and the official June 2026 REST contract no longer matches the CLI type; live ENV verification also found an explicit-false safety regression.
